questions: Verify print mode, sessions, automatic context compaction and schema/report extraction.
Check accounting, interruption and permission boundaries against pinned upstream code.
decision: Make Kimi prompt-mode permission behavior an explicit versioned compatibility decision; reject unsupported safe-role invocations instead of silently deleting flags.
code_observations: The existing Kimi worker appends a configured permission flag and --prompt. The current official command reference says --prompt cannot be combined with --yolo, --auto or --plan.

The legacy reference instead documents --print and its own non-interactive semantics. This is a documentation/source incompatibility risk, not a reproduced failure of an installed CLI in this environment.
implementation_steps: Introduce bounded version/help discovery and explicit supported protocol variants. Never combine flags from the old and new references.
For a current variant, construct the documented non-interactive invocation and handle its permission boundary explicitly; for a legacy variant, retain only the tested compatible syntax.
Normalize stream-json messages into terminal outcome, bounded report and usage. Intermediate text, context-compaction events and tool output are not a completion artifact.
Treat session reuse as opt-in with documented storage/retention; default cross-provider continuation remains an evidence capsule and the worktree.
Add a diagnostic that identifies unknown versions without silently switching to unrestricted operation. Preserve user configuration and never run an automatic upgrade.
Version Kimi prompt and permission combinations; never repair an invocation by silently broadening permissions.
Bind any explicit resume to the exact task and repository, including saved permission state.
Disable advisory roles when a genuine read-only boundary cannot be established.
proposed_acceptance_tests: Current fixtures reject --prompt combined with obsolete or mutually exclusive permission flags.
Legacy fixtures keep their documented print-mode syntax instead of receiving current-only flags.
A missing terminal report, malformed JSONL or interrupted stream cannot pass acceptance.
Budget, transient and permanent errors are normalized only when the version contract establishes their meaning.
Session identifiers and logs never introduce secrets into a shared handoff.
Prompt plus obsolete permission flags yields a compatibility failure before model work.
Fallback flag removal cannot change the authorized permission profile.
Resume cannot inherit another task saved permissions.
Native exit zero with missing completion schema is rejected.

cost_model: Fail fast on incompatible arguments rather than spending retries or escalating the model. Session reuse is an experiment with privacy/reconstruction costs, not the default optimization.
unverified: No installed Kimi executable was run, so actual compatibility must be confirmed with its version/help and one bounded authorized test.
No Kimi executable or authenticated run was performed. The observed documentation describes current behavior and must be reconciled with the installed version.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated provider invocation, live quota/cost benchmark, independent model review, or Windows runtime test was performed in this research revision.
previous_decision: Add version-aware Kimi command contracts before changing flags: the current and legacy documentation describe materially different non-interactive modes.
revision_delta: The current official reference changes the meaning and permitted combinations of yolo/auto/plan with prompt. A mechanical removal of a rejected flag could accidentally broaden execution permissions.
decision_analysis: The existing adapter should not treat yolo as a timeless synonym for auto-approval across versions. The inspected guide makes prompt mode incompatible with yolo, auto and plan flags and gives it an automatic permission mode. Probe or pin the contract; do not blindly retry a failed invocation with those flags removed.

For implementation workers, automatic permission may be allowed only inside the user-authorized filesystem/process boundary. For review and monitoring, a prompt-mode planner preference is not a proven read-only boundary. Reject the optional role when the installed Kimi configuration cannot enforce its restrictions.

Session reuse must bind a known session id to repository, task and provider. Resuming a latest session can import unrelated state, saved permissions or model selection. Keep fresh workers as the default and document persistence/cleanup implications separately from accepted model output.

Structured final report validation and runner-owned tests remain mandatory even if the native CLI exits successfully. Capture partial output and stderr without treating them as instructions or leaking credentials. Compatibility errors belong in a bounded preflight or environment path, not in a costly model escalation loop.

ownership: This implementation owns its declared write scope and acceptance tests. Its following review checks the actual changed code; prepared research is not acceptance evidence.
baseline_anchor_check: All listed file hashes matched the preserved 0.11.0 source in this revision. This is integrity checking, not a second full code audit.
applicability_rule: Refresh only evidence contradicted by the installed CLI, selected account/billing plan or changed code contract. Unknown required capability blocks that candidate; it does not justify widening permissions.
